name: Aranmula Kannadi — the Metal Mirror
tagline: A hand-cast metal-alloy mirror made only in Aranmula
summary: Aranmula Kannadi: Kerala's famous hand-cast metal mirror, its history and legend, how to spot an authentic piece, and where to buy and see it made.
description: The Aranmula kannadi is a polished metal-alloy mirror made by a small number of families in Aranmula, a temple town on the Pamba river. Unlike glass mirrors it reflects from the front surface, so there is no ghost image.
The exact alloy and polishing method are traditionally guarded as a family craft. Aranmula kannadi holds a Geographical Indication tag and is used as a lucky object in ceremonies.

history.significance: One of Kerala's most distinctive crafts, tied to the Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple and the ritual life of the town.

timeline.event: Local legend places the craft among artisans brought to serve the Aranmula temple.
The craft survives through a few families and cooperative bodies.
Aranmula Kannadi receives Geographical Indication protection, helping buyers identify authentic pieces.

keyFacts: The mirror is front-surfaced, which gives a sharp, undistorted reflection.
It is made by a small number of artisan families; production is slow.
One of the items placed in the ashtamangalyam set, auspicious articles used in ceremonies.
Real pieces are sold with tags or certificates; check the seller's credentials.

folklore.title: The Mirror of the Temple
story: Tradition says the first kannadi was made by a group of skilled metalworkers who came to Aranmula to serve the Parthasarathy Temple, and that the secret alloy was entrusted to their families.
Another story says the king of Travancore valued the mirror so highly that he placed it among the auspicious items offered at royal ceremonies.
folklore.note: Oral accounts differ; origin is traditional, not documented history.

spiritual.summary: The mirror is treated as an auspicious object that brings clarity and good fortune into a home.

experiences.title: Visit a workshop
experiences.text: At a family workshop you can see polishing, which takes patient, repeated work.

experiences.title: Attend the Aranmula temple festival season
experiences.text: The town comes alive during the Uthrattathi boat race and the Vallasadya feast; check dates.

mindfulTips: Handle the mirror gently; scratches are hard to repair.
Respect the workshop's request about photographing the process.

highlights: Front-surface metal mirror with no ghost image
Pamba river and the Uthrattathi boat race

visitorInfo.bestTime: October to March; boat race and temple festivals fall in August–September.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Aranmula is on the Pamba river near Chengannur; the nearest railhead is Chengannur (CNGR), about 10 km away.
etiquette: Buy only from certified workshops or cooperatives.
Do not bargain in temple precincts.

heritage.materials: Copper-tin based metal alloy (exact formula guarded)

whereToSee.name: Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple
whereToSee.note: Centre of the town's festivals and the Uthrattathi boat race.

whereToBuy.name: Aranmula Vishwabrahma Handicrafts Co-operative / Aranmula Kannadi workshops
whereToBuy.note: Buy from certified outlets with a Geographical Indication tag or certificate (verify the current society and shops).

whereToBuy.name: Kairali — Kerala State Handicrafts Apex Co-operative Society emporiums
whereToBuy.note: Government-linked craft emporiums in major towns; fixed prices and craft-certified items.

experiences.name: Aranmula Heritage Village / Vijnana Kalavedi
experiences.note: Cultural initiatives promoting Aranmula's crafts and arts (verify current visiting arrangements).

buyingTips: Insist on a tag or certificate and a written guarantee.
Prices are high; very cheap 'Aranmula mirrors' are imitations.
Take the piece in protective packing for travel.

images.alt: Aranmula kannadi, meaning the Aranmula mirror, is a handmade metal-alloy mirror, made in Aranmula, a small town in Pathanamthitta, Kerala, India.
